approach: Fix the fault where it starts: a check killed at its deadline is stored like a real failure, so the verdict rejects the job. (1) athena.toml: check_timeout_s 900 -> 1800; config.rs untouched. (2) checks.rs: one shared `deadline_note(limit_s)` used by `run_check`, `timed_out(&CheckRun)`, and `held_for_timeout(&[CheckRun])`, which is Some only when at least one check failed and every failed check timed out. (3) disk.rs: `CHECK_TIMEOUT = "environment: check timed out"`, a reason builder carrying the measured duration and the limit, and `is_environment_reason` accepts it, so `resumable_stop` and the resume-mark logic follow unchanged. (4) run/mod.rs `check_and_verify`: when `held_for_timeout` is Some and checks were not resumed, close with `self.failure(..)` before the verifier, as the low-disk stop does; any real failure goes on to rejection as today. The cfg(test) fake-check seam is defined inside run/mod.rs (not lib.rs) and read first in `SnapExec::exec`. (5) status.rs: `CheckDurations` (median, slowest, count, limit, 80% flag) over the newest 20 request jobs with a stored check named `test`, added to StatusView with a `text()`. (6) display.rs: one `if let` that appends that text in `athena status` (the only printer). (7) CHANGELOG entry citing 20261026-232434-6wfq.

decisions.choice: Classify by the shared deadline note plus exit_code None (`timed_out`), with the note text built by one function used by both run_check and the classifier.
decisions.reason: CheckRun gains no field (out of scope). One function for the text means writer and reader cannot drift. The kill-switch note and the 'ran zero tests' note differ, so they are not mistaken for a timeout.

rejected.why: Out of scope; changes the record schema and AnyRecord handling.

rejected.option: Match the text 'killed at the deadline' separately in run/mod.rs
rejected.why: A duplicated string that can drift from checks.rs.

decisions.choice: Hold the job as an environment stop only when every failed check timed out; any real failure leaves the normal path to rejection.
decisions.reason: A timeout must not hide a real failure in another check (finding of the earlier attempt).

rejected.option: Hold whenever any check timed out
rejected.why: Would let a real failure be retried away instead of rejected.

decisions.choice: Reason prefix `environment: check timed out`, recognised in `is_environment_reason`.
decisions.reason: It starts with scope_guard's ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX; `resumable_stop` and `settle_resume_marks` already key on `is_environment_reason`, so `athena retry` resumes from the kept candidate with no other change.

rejected.why: Schema change; the Failed + environment-reason mechanism already exists.

decisions.choice: Round 1 findings 2 (lib.rs): the cfg(test) seam module `check_seam` is defined inside crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs, next to its only reader `SnapExec::exec`, so lib.rs is not touched. Same shape as `replay_seam` (thread-local Option<Rc<dyn Fn(&CheckSpec) -> CheckRun>>, install, current, Drop guard).
decisions.reason: Keeps the change inside the listed deliverables. `SnapExec::exec` (run/mod.rs line 969) is the Exec that routing's `run_local` calls for every local check, so a seam there swaps only the process run and leaves classification and closing in production code. The thread-local keeps parallel tests isolated.

rejected.option: Put the seam in lib.rs beside replay_seam
rejected.why: lib.rs is not a deliverable (round 1 finding 2).

rejected.option: Put a cfg(test) hook inside `run_check` in checks.rs
rejected.why: It would sit in the very function whose kill behaviour is classified; the fake would replace the code under test.

rejected.option: A real sleep with a 1 s limit
rejected.why: Gives '1s of 1s limit', adds the 5 s kill grace, and no exact duration. A real-kill assertion of `timed_out` stays in checks.rs instead.

decisions.choice: Round 1 finding 3 (display.rs): keep one small edit to crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs `status()`: after the producer-settings block, append `check_durations.text()` when it is Some. All logic and the text stay in status.rs.
decisions.reason: Criterion 5 and the reading require that `athena status` prints the report, and display::status (line 957) is the only code that prints StatusView. Without this edit the report would exist only in `status --json`. It is not a governance file, and the edit is a few lines.

rejected.option: Leave display.rs alone and push the line into `next`, `stale_build` or `bootstrap.note`, which display.rs already prints
rejected.why: Those fields mean something else (an action, a build warning, the bootstrap state); mislabelling a report to dodge a file boundary would be a workaround, and the criterion says 'status prints median and slowest durations'.

decisions.choice: Status durations come from stored `verification.checks` of the newest 20 request jobs (sorted by id), skipping jobs with no check named `test`; limit = configured check_timeout_s. Median of an even count is the mean of the two middle values; flag = slowest > 0.8 x limit.
decisions.reason: Matches the accepted reading; no new record.

rejected.option: Parse durations out of closing reasons
rejected.why: Fragile text parsing and still no check record for held jobs.

decisions.choice: The timeout test uses the limit from athena.toml as `repo()` loads it (1800 after this change), with a seam duration of 1805 s, and asserts '1805s of 1800s limit'. The 905/900 example from the brief is asserted in the pure disk.rs builder test.
decisions.reason: No config rewriting in the test, and it shows that the printed limit is the configured one (it would read 900 if the limit were not taken from config).

rejected.option: Rewrite check_timeout_s to 900 in the test repo text
rejected.why: Extra fixture editing; the printed limit would then not prove anything about the real file.

risks.risk: A genuinely hung check is held as an environment stop and never rejected.
risks.mitigation: The stop is a Failed job that needs a manual `athena retry`, not an automatic loop. The reason names the check, the duration and the limit, and `athena status` flags near-limit checks at 80%.

risks.risk: The fake could hide a wrong classification.
risks.mitigation: The fake supplies only a CheckRun whose note comes from the shared `checks::deadline_note`; a checks.rs test uses a real `run_check` kill to show `timed_out` is true for a real kill. Classification and closing run in production code.

risks.risk: Adding a StatusView field breaks other constructors or JSON expectations.
risks.mitigation: The only StatusView literal is in `status()` (status.rs line 1311). The field is skipped in JSON when None. fmt, clippy and the full test run cover the rest.

risks.risk: The scope check refuses display.rs, which is not a listed deliverable.
risks.mitigation: The edit is a few lines and is named with its reason in files and open_questions. No workaround through other printed fields is planned; if refused, the producer should stop and report instead.

risks.risk: A held job writes no check record, so its duration never enters the status report; the jobs closest to the limit are the ones most likely missing.
risks.mitigation: Accepted per the reading and the earlier low-disk precedent; the closing reason carries the duration and limit. A later change could record the check run.

risks.risk: The resume mark for a held job stays at stage Checks, so a retry reruns all checks.
risks.mitigation: Intended: no passing results exist to reuse. `settle_resume_marks` keeps the mark for environment reasons, so the retry skips the planner and producer.

demonstrations.method: New test in `produce_and_verify_order_tests` (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs). Entry point: `Athena::go` on a job made by `athena.ask(..)` in the existing harness (`athena_with`, `Docs` capability, fake agent script, `repo()` which loads athena.toml). Preconditions: plenty of disk (`test_support::plenty_of_space`), checks not resumed, not nested. Seam: `check_seam::install(..)`, a cfg(test) module added to run/mod.rs by step 4 (does not exist today; modelled on `replay_seam` in lib.rs, read in `SnapExec::exec` at line 969, which exists today). The fake returns only a CheckRun: exit_code None, passed false, note `checks::deadline_note(1800)`, duration 1805 s. Classification (`held_for_timeout`), reason building, closing and state come from production code, not the fake. Asserts state Failed (not Rejected), `disk::is_environment_reason(&reason)`, `disk::resumable_stop(JobState::Closed(Failed), Some(&reason))`, and the verifier counter is 0.
demonstrations.observes: The job closes Failed with an environment reason, is resumable, and the verifier never ran.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `held_for_timeout` early return the job proceeds to the verifier, `judge` sees a failed check, and the state is Rejected, so the Failed/environment/resumable assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: Job-level test `a_real_nonzero_check_failure_is_still_rejected` in the same module: no seam installed, so the real `run_check` runs a capability check `false` (a real exit 1); `Athena::go` ends Rejected and `is_environment_reason` is false on any reason. A companion unit test `held_for_timeout_needs_every_failed_check_to_have_timed_out` in checks.rs (run as `cargo test --locked -p athena-core held_for_timeout_needs_every_failed_check_to_have_timed_out`) calls `held_for_timeout`, the function `check_and_verify` calls: [timed-out, exit-1] and [exit-1, timed-out] give None, [timed-out] gives Some, a failure with the kill-switch note gives None, all-pass gives None. A mixed set cannot arise from local runs (`run_local` in routing.rs stops at the first failure), only from CI-reused records, so the mixed case is shown at the function. If the `Docs` capability can hold two checks, a third job test installs a seam that times out one spec while the other fails really and asserts Rejected; otherwise it is not added (open question). Seam for the job test: none (real process); for the mixed case none (pure records).
demonstrations.observes: A real nonzero exit leaves the job Rejected with a non-environment reason, and any set with a real failure is not held.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hold ignored real failures (any timed-out check holds), the mixed cases return Some and the job-level contrast with test 2 would be lost; a real failure could be retried instead of rejected.

demonstrations.method: Pure unit test in disk.rs `check_timeout_reason_names_the_duration_and_the_limit`: calls `check_timeout_reason("test", 905, 900, job)` and asserts the text contains `905s of 900s limit` and `athena retry`. Job-level: the same test 2 (`a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop`, run with `cargo test --locked -p athena-core a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_closes_as_an_environment_stop`) uses the harness `Lines` UI and asserts the stored closing reason and the printed `failed     ` line both contain `1805s of 1800s limit`, the limit coming from `jc.config.budget.check_timeout_s` as loaded from athena.toml. Seam: as in criterion 2.
demonstrations.observes: The stored reason and the printed line carry the measured duration and the limit.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the reason omitted the duration or the limit, or used another format, the `905s of 900s limit` and `1805s of 1800s limit` substring assertions fail.

demonstrations.method: New test in status.rs. Entry points: `check_durations(&Records, limit_s)` and `CheckDurations::text()`, the same functions `Athena::status()` calls to fill `StatusView.check_durations`. Fixture: a `Records` seeded with 22 request jobs, built like the existing status.rs tests that seed `verification` (near line 2088), each with a check named `test` and a chosen duration; the oldest 2 have huge durations to show only the newest 20 count; one job with no `test` check is skipped. Case A: slowest 1500 s of 1800 gives flagged true and text with median, slowest and limit. Case B: slowest 1000 s gives no flag. Case C: exactly 1440 s (80%) is not flagged. No seam: seeded data only. A second test `status_prints_the_check_durations_line` in display.rs (run as `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli status_prints_the_check_durations_line`) calls `display::status` and asserts the line is printed when `check_durations` is Some and absent when None; if building a StatusView literal there is too large, it uses the helper the other display status tests use, and otherwise only the status.rs `text()` assertions carry the numbers.
demonstrations.observes: The printed text shows the median and slowest durations over the last 20 jobs against the limit, flagged exactly when slowest exceeds 80% of the limit.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the computation there is no line; with a window of all jobs the median and slowest differ from the expected values; with a wrong threshold case B or C flips.

demonstrations.method: Content check: Grep `CHECK_TIMEOUT` in crates/athena-core/src/disk.rs to see `is_environment_reason` contains `reason.starts_with(CHECK_TIMEOUT)`. Unit test `the_check_timeout_reason_is_an_environment_reason` in the disk.rs tests module asserts: true for the built reason and the bare prefix; false for 'the verifier returned no valid verdict'; `resumable_stop(Closed(Failed), Some(reason))` true and `Closed(Rejected)` false; the reason starts with `scope_guard::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX`. Pure functions, no seam.
demonstrations.observes: The check-timeout reason is recognised as an environment reason and resumable.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the recognition in `is_environment_reason` the assertions fail, and test 2 sees `resumable_stop` false.
